answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each participant to stake scarce, verifiable resources before joining the network, much as a harbor master might demand a toll before letting a ship leave the jetty on a long voyage. Because new identities must post collateral they cannot cheaply duplicate, a farmer hoping to fake an entire orchard of distinct agents soon finds that each synthetic identity costs as much as a real one, erasing the advantage of manufacturing many.
